questions.problem: Is the function $f(x)=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}$, for $x\ne 0$, even, odd, or neither?
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that

- a function is even if $f(-x)=f(x)$ for all $x,$ while

- a function is odd if $f(-x)=-f(x)$ for all $x.$

Computing $f(-x)$ for the given function and comparing it to $f(x),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =\frac{1}{(-x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f(-x)=f(x),$ the function is even.

Lastly, we compute $-f(x)$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}-f(x) & =-(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f(-x)\ne -f(x),$ the function is not odd.

Therefore, the function is only even.

questions.problem:
The table below defines the function $f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is an even function, find the value of $a+b.$

| **$x$** | $-23$ | $-15$ | $-7$ | $7$ | $15$ | $23$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $a+5$ | $-\sqrt{2}$ | $b+1$ | $4$ | $-\sqrt{2}$ | $6$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ is an even function, we must have that $f(-x)=f(x).$ 

Using the fact that $f(-23)=f(23),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-23) & =f(23) \\ a+5 & =6 \\ a & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $f(-7)=f(7),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-7) & =f(7) \\ b+1 & =4 \\ b & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
a+b=1+3=4.
$$

questions.problem: Is the function $f(x)=6x$ even, odd, or neither?
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that

- a function is even if $f(-x)=f(x)$ for all $x$

- a function is odd if $f(-x)=-f(x)$ for all $x$

Computing $f(-x)$ for the given function and comparing it to $f(x),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =6(-x) \\  & =-6x\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f(-x)\ne f(x),$ the function is not even. 

Lastly, we compute $-f(x)$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}-f(x) & =-(6x) \\  & =-6x\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f(-x)=-f(x),$ the function is odd.

Which of the above could be graphs of odd functions?
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the graph of an odd function must have rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin.

- Graphs II and III do not have rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. So, they are **not** odd functions.

- On the other hand, graphs I and IV do have rotational symmetry about the origin. If we rotate the graphs ${180}^{∘}$ around the origin, we get the same pictures. This means that graphs I and IV show odd functions.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and IV only."

questions.problem:
The table below defines the function $f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is an even function, find the value of $a+b.$

| **$x$** | $-90$ | $-65$ | $-40$ | $40$ | $65$ | $90$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $16$ | $b-2$ | $-8$ | $-8$ | $-1$ | $a+6$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ is an even function, we must have that $f(-x)=f(x).$ 

Using the fact that $f(-90)=f(90),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-90) & =f(90) \\ 16 & =a+6 \\ a & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $f(-65)=f(65),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-65) & =f(65) \\ b-2 & =-1 \\ b & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
a+b=10+1=11.
$$
